knowledge:
- key_parameters: rmNegProbe=logical, whether to remove negative probes during data import in readGeoMx ;; rm_genes=logical, whether to remove non-expressed genes during ROI-level QC in addPerROIQC ;; ordannots=character, the column name in colData used to order samples/ROIs in QC and RLE plots ;; y_threshold=numeric, the library size threshold for filtering out low-quality ROIs in plotROIQC ;; method=character, the normalization method to use in geomxNorm (options: "TMM", "RPKM", "TPM", "CPM", "upperquartile", "sizefactor") ;; batch_name=character, the colData column representing the batch variable (e.g., "SlideName") in findNCGs ;; top_n=numeric, the number of least variable genes across batches to select as negative control genes (NCGs) ;; factors=character, the biological factors to preserve during batch correction in geomxBatchCorrection ;; NCGs=character vector, negative control genes used for RUV4 batch correction ;; k=numeric, the number of factors of unwanted variation to remove in geomxBatchCorrection
- alternatives: Normalization methods include TMM, RPKM, TPM, CPM, upperquartile, and sizefactor. RPKM and TPM should only be preferred when gene length information is available and added to the rowData of the object.
- when_to_use: Use this workflow when analyzing NanoString GeoMx DSP transcriptomics data, particularly when multiple slides introduce batch effects that need to be corrected using RUV4 while preserving biological variation.
- pitfalls: Collinearity in region-related annotations can negatively affect batch correction; annotations should be merged or simplified before running batch correction. RPKM and TPM normalization methods will fail if the "genelength" column is not manually added to the rowData of the SpatialExperiment object. Low-quality ROIs with low library sizes (e.g., < 50000) must be filtered out to avoid skewing downstream normalization and batch correction.

workflows.name: geomx_dsp_qc_norm_batch_correction
workflows.intent: Perform quality control, TMM normalization, and RUV4 batch correction on NanoString GeoMx DSP data.
workflows.stages: 1. Import raw GeoMx data ;; 2. Preprocess metadata to avoid collinearity ;; 3. Perform gene-level QC ;; 4. Perform ROI-level QC and filter low-quality ROIs ;; 5. Inspect variations using RLE and PCA ;; 6. Normalize data using TMM ;; 7. Identify Negative Control Genes (NCGs) ;; 8. Perform RUV4 batch correction ;; 9. Visualize corrected data
workflows.code:
spe <- readGeoMx(countFile, sampleAnnoFile, featureAnnoFile = featureAnnoFile, rmNegProbe = TRUE)

colData(spe)$regions <- paste0(colData(spe)$region,"_",colData(spe)$SegmentLabel) |> 
  (\(.) gsub("_Geometric Segment","",.))() |>
  paste0("_",colData(spe)$pathology) |>
  (\(.) gsub("_NA","_ns",.))()

library(ggalluvial)

plotSampleInfo(spe, column2plot = c("SlideName","disease_status","regions"))

spe <- addPerROIQC(spe, rm_genes = TRUE)

plotGeneQC(spe, ordannots = "regions", col = regions, point_size = 2)

plotROIQC(spe, y_threshold = 50000, col = SlideName)

spe <- spe[,rownames(colData(spe))[colData(spe)$lib_size > 50000]]

plotRLExpr(spe, ordannots = "SlideName", assay = 2, col = SlideName)

drawPCA(spe, assay = 2, col = SlideName, shape = regions)

colData(spe)$biology <- paste0(colData(spe)$disease_status, "_", colData(spe)$regions)

spe_tmm <- geomxNorm(spe, method = "TMM")

spe <- findNCGs(spe, batch_name = "SlideName", top_n = 500)

metadata(spe) |> names()

spe_ruv <- geomxBatchCorrection(spe, factors = "biology", 
                   NCGs = metadata(spe)$NCGs, k = 5)

plotPairPCA(spe_ruv, assay = 2, color = disease_status, shape = regions, title = "RUV4")

plotRLExpr(spe_ruv, assay = 2, color = SlideName) + ggtitle("RUV4")
